title: Simulation

match.reason: The bank point teaches discrete probability distributions, a different idea from estimating a probability by simulating a chance process with random numbers, so no bank point matches the new point.

draft.title: Simulation
card: A simulation uses random numbers to act out a chance process again and again. Each run is called a trial.
First, decide how random digits stand for the outcomes. If a chance is 30%, let 3 of the 10 digits 0 to 9 stand for it, such as 0, 1 and 2.
Then run many trials and count how often the event happens. Estimated probability = number of trials with the event ÷ total number of trials.
Example: a bus is late 30% of the time. In 50 simulated days it is late on 14 days. The estimate is 14 ÷ 50 = 0.28. More trials usually give a more reliable estimate.
draft.remember: Assign digits to match the chances, run many trials, then divide the successes by the trials.

a.q: A shop's card reader fails 20% of the time. Which digit rule matches this for one random digit from 0 to 9?
a.why: Two of the ten digits give 2 ÷ 10 = 20%. Digit 2 alone gives 10%, and digits 0 to 4 give 50%.
a.clue: Count how many of the ten digits you need for 20%.

b.q: Priya simulates a free-throw shooter who scores 70% of the time. In 40 trials, she gets a score in 30 of them. What is her estimated probability of a score?
b.why: Estimate = 30 ÷ 40 = 0.75. It differs from 0.70 because simulations vary. Dividing 40 by 30 would give 1.33, which cannot be a probability.
b.clue: Divide the trials with the event by all the trials.
